title: DKA 1 of 7, PICU to adolescent unit: new-onset type 1 diabetes in severe DKA (3 days, checkpoints every 0700 and 1900)
diagnosis: New-onset type 1 diabetes presenting in severe diabetic ketoacidosis (pH 7.04, bicarbonate 5, anion gap 28, glucose 612), about 8% dehydration with AKI; possible cerebral edema on Day 1; hypokalemia and hypophosphatemia; night hypoglycemia after the transition
desc: Mon 12/07 0700 to Thu 12/10 0700. A 16-year-old with 5 weeks of thirst, peeing and weight loss arrives in the PICU in severe DKA. Pediatric protocol (one 10 mL/kg bolus, insulin 0.1 unit/kg/h without bolus, two-bag dextrose, potassium and phosphate), cerebral edema signs at 1130 treated with mannitol, low potassium with U waves, DKA resolved overnight, transition to glargine and lispro, a night low after a bedtime correction, then CGM, glucagon, sick-day and school teaching with her parents. Vital signs after 0700 come from the bedside monitor.
